intro: A banjo player with a shifting cast of bandmates.
story: Danny Barnes brought his Collective, one of his shape-shifting ensembles, to Pickathon in 2005, the year Get Myself Together came out on Terminus Records. The album covered the rural bluesman Willie Johnson alongside the Rolling Stones. In 2016 he paid homage to banjo player Don Stover on Stove Up, his return to traditional bluegrass.

intro: A Portland old-time band with a punk drive.
story: The Dickel Brothers, a Portland old-time band that began when Matt Dickel and a friend started busking in 1996, played Pickathon in 2005. Volume One, their first full-length, came out on the indie-punk label Empty Records that year, and No Depression reviewed it.

intro: A Portland trio of three songwriters.
story: Dirty Martini, the Portland trio of Lara Michell, Stephanie Schneiderman and McKinley, took its name from a first gig spent on salty drinks. The band played Pickathon in 2005, the year its self-titled debut came out, and followed with Tea and Revenge. The three formed Swan Sovereign in 2013, and in February 2024 Dirty Martini opened a Swan Sovereign show at Mendelssohns.

intro: A Portland old-time band that began at a fiddle contest.
story: Foghorn Stringband began with campfire jams at the National Oldtime Fiddlers' Contest in Weiser, Idaho, in 2000, under the name Foghorn Leghorn, and grew out of a Sunday residency at a Portland pub, the Moon and Sixpence. They played Pickathon in 2005. Reeb Willms joined in the winter of 2011.

intro: A Louisville duo of dark country harmonies.
story: Freakwater, the Louisville duo of Catherine Irwin and Janet Bean, first recorded their harmonies in the basement of Bean's parents' house in 1985, and played Pickathon in 2005, the year Thinking of You came out on Thrill Jockey. Scheherazade, their first studio album in a decade, followed on Bloodshot in 2016.

intro: A western-soul band built by two California songwriters.
story: The Hacienda Brothers, the western-soul band of Chris Gaffney and Dave Gonzalez, began in 2002 as a jam at a friend's 40th birthday party. They played Pickathon in 2005, the year their self-titled debut came out on Koch, produced by Dan Penn, and returned in 2007. Gaffney died in 2008.

Jackstraw, the Portland bluegrass band, played Pickathon in 2005, one of its seven visits. Guitarist Jon Neufeld, who also plays with Black Prairie and Martha Scanlan, later produced Smithsonian Folkways' Roll Columbia: Woody Guthrie's 26 Northwest Songs, released in January 2017.

intro: A Texas-born songwriter who helped start The Be Good Tanyas.
story: Jolie Holland, the Houston-born songwriter who helped found The Be Good Tanyas, played Pickathon in 2005, a year after Escondida, her first album for Anti-. Tom Waits, a fan, put her debut Catalpa up for the Shortlist Music Prize. In 2017 she reunited with Be Good Tanyas bandmate Samantha Parton for Wildflower Blues.
Jug Free America, a Northwest string band, played Pickathon in 2005.

Mary Flower, a fingerstyle guitarist who moved from Denver to Portland in 2004, played Pickathon in 2005. She was nominated for Blues Music Awards in 2008, 2012 and 2016, and the Cascade Blues Association inducted her into its Hall of Fame in 2018. Folk Alliance Region West named her its Best of the West Artist in 2025.
Rosie Brown, a local folk singer, played Pickathon in 2005.

intro: A Northwest string band named for a fiddle tune.
story: Sandy River Belle, a Pacific Northwest string band, played Pickathon in 2005.

The Be Good Tanyas, the Vancouver trio of Frazey Ford, Samantha Parton and Trish Klein, played Pickathon in 2005, after Blue Horse on Nettwerk and Chinatown in 2003. Jolie Holland left before Blue Horse but appears on it. A Ford song, "In Spite of All the Damage," was used on the Showtime series The L Word, and her solo debut, Obadiah, followed in 2010.

intro: A dark-toned San Francisco old-time band.
story: The Crooked Jades, founded in San Francisco in 1994 by Jeff Kazor and Lisa Berman, played Pickathon in 2003, 2005 and 2007. Berman also co-founded the Stairwell Sisters, and Kazor co-founded the San Francisco Bluegrass and Old-Time Festival in 1999. Their song "World's on Fire" was used in the 2007 film Into the Wild.

intro: A San Francisco old-time banjo band.
story: The Earl Brothers, a San Francisco old-time band led by Robert Earl Davis, played Pickathon in 2005 and returned in 2006.
The Hunger Mountain Boys, a Massachusetts old-time duet of Teddy Weber and Matt Downing, played Pickathon in 2005 and again in 2007.
The Shiftless Rounders, an old-time string band, played Pickathon in 2004 and 2005 and appeared on a live compilation from the festival.

intro: A folk singer who had been half of a Portland duo.
story: Tracy Grammer was half of the Portland folk duo Dave Carter and Tracy Grammer until Carter died in July 2002. She played Pickathon in 2005, the year she took over administering his catalog and released Flower of Avalon. Little Blue Egg, on Red House in 2012, gathered 11 unreleased duo recordings.
